title: Blast Radius — agent narrative input
description: The plain-language half of a blast radius report. Written by the Blast Radius Analyst agent to .github/.pipeline-context/blast-radius/<issue_id>.narrative.json after reading the facts briefing, then consumed by scripts/render-blast-radius.js. Write for a reader who has not seen the code: no class names where a capability name will do, no jargon where a plain word exists. Every claim must stay inside the reach the collector measured.

issue_id.description: Must match the id in the facts file, e.g. ISSUE-001.

confidence.description: How certain the reach assessment is. Low when it depends on runtime conditions the code cannot show, such as data volume or traffic.

scope.description: How wide the failure really is — this drives which endpoints the report marks as down. 'endpoint': the service still runs, only the paths that execute the defect fail. 'service': the whole service is unavailable (it cannot build, cannot start, or exhausts its resources), so every endpoint it hosts is down. 'multi-service': more than one service is directly broken, not merely degraded. Choose from the root cause, not from the symptom.

headline.description: One sentence a non-engineer would understand, stating what stops working. Rendered as the quote under the title.

what_is_broken.description: A short paragraph in plain language: what fails, when it fails, and whether it fails every time or only under certain conditions.

same_service.description: What else inside the broken service stops working, and why. One or two sentences.

dependent_services.description: What happens to services that call the broken one. Name them. If nothing calls it, say so plainly.

wider_platform.description: Optional. Effects on shared infrastructure — the database, config server, discovery server — or on services that merely share them.

user_impact.description: Who notices, and what they see. Describe roles and journeys, not code.

who.description: The affected group, e.g. 'HR administrators', 'Payroll reporting', 'Any API client'.

what_they_see.description: The observable experience, e.g. 'The save button returns an error and no department is created.'

status.description: Blocked: cannot complete the task at all. Degraded: completes but with wrong, missing or slow results. At risk: fine today, fails as conditions change.

failure_note.description: Optional. Short label for the failure point in the request-path diagram, e.g. 'recurses instead of saving'. Keep under about 60 characters.

not_affected.description: What keeps working. Scoping the damage is as valuable as describing it — call out intact capabilities, unaffected data, and anything a reader might wrongly assume is broken.

containment.description: What to do before the fix ships: what to disable, monitor, communicate, or route around. Actions, not analysis.

priority.description: A priority with a reason attached, e.g. 'P1 — blocks a core write path, fix before the next release'.

if_unfixed.description: What gets worse over time if this ships or stays in production.

open_questions.description: Anything the code and graph cannot settle — traffic levels, data volumes, network exposure, client retry behaviour. Use this instead of guessing.
